preamble: The solutions to four partial clues are distinctly uncomplicated

clue.text: See 23
Deadly stretch of high ground

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective is fierce or lethal, as in one ... swoop
a hill or moorland upland in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses: an archaic adjective for lethal and a northern English noun for upland moor.

clue.text: Almost sick-looking sailor in drink is nice!

indicators.note: in says the sailor and colour pieces sit inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a beer

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: someone queasy is said to look green
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A seasick sailor having a drink declares it lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims GREEN to GREE; with AB it goes 'in' ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreeable is pleasant, the everyday sense of nice.

clue.text: To isolate some men is legitimate

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Separating a few men off is perfectly lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: To enisle is a poetic verb meaning to place on an island, cutting off from others.

clue.text: Recoil brings disadvantage

definitions.meaning: to ... is to shrink away or recoil

explanation.walkthrough: Recoil asks for DRAW BACK, two words; the grid joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means flinch away; as one noun it means a downside or snag.

clue.text: Character involved with Easter arrangement — intellect or a dim lunatic?

indicators.note: lunatic suggests letters behaving madly, so the four words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is a brainbox or a crazy dimwit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominical letter is the letter A to G marking Sundays in a year, used when working out the date of Easter.

clue.text: A sort of host with great collection of books next door

parts.note: a disc jockey hosts a radio show or club night
ace is slang for excellent
NT is the New Testament, a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: A radio presenter living beside a huge library.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent describes something lying beside, as a neighbouring house does.

clue.text: Where's the feeling that could make Maureen cry when upset

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the pieces so they read bottom to top

parts.note: Mo is a familiar short form of Maureen
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Something that would make a woman called Maureen weep in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: The breast is traditionally the seat of emotions, as in a heart and soul figure of speech.

clue.text: The non-work element essential to early years development

definitions.text: The non-work element essential to early years development

parts.words: The non-work element essential to early years development
parts.note: describes the playing infants do as they grow, phrased like nursery-education jargon

explanation.surface: A line from an education policy paper on toddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, this answer also means very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Play is what small children do instead of work, and it helps them develop; the idiom also means a trivial task.

clue.text: Liar must reform to show generosity to others

indicators.note: a reform reshapes the letters of the liar and must words into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest person has to mend their ways and become kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for the wellbeing of other people.

clue.text: Religious type? In Paris I'll go to clubs, maybe!

parts.note: je is French for the pronoun I
clubs is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A Frenchman saying he will head off to nightspots.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit is a member of the Society of Jesus, a Catholic order.

clue.text: Grey old cinema somehow not right for classic film?

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are jumbled in some way
not says one letter is left out of the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A drab, ageing picture house is somehow wrong for showing an old classic.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from GREY OLD CINEMA ('not right') and 'somehow' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing comedies were celebrated British films from Ealing Studios in London, mostly made 1947 to 1957.

clue.text: No case for this person making a short excursion

definitions.text: No case for this person making a short excursion

parts.words: No case for this person making a short excursion
parts.note: someone out and back within a day needs no suitcase

explanation.surface: Advice that a quick outing needs no luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A day tripper makes an excursion returning the same day, so packs no bag.

clue.text: Fish counter, Billingsgate's first

parts.note: a bar is a serving counter

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the market's name

explanation.surface: A fish slab at the London fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's famous fish market.
explanation.definitionFit: The barb is a small freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: In court, performing secretary maybe shows disdain for legal procedure

indicators.note: in places the performing and secretary pieces inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: on means on stage, performing
a temp is a temporary office worker such as a secretary

explanation.surface: An agency secretary acting up in a courtroom shows scorn for the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is wilful disrespect towards a court's authority.

clue.text: Start of exercise, say, repeatedly cavorting round gym

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the next word
round puts the two copies either side of the gym piece
repeatedly means the jumbled piece appears twice over
cavorting means prancing about, so the letters of say are moved around

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym class

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor's patter about leaping round a gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' scrambles SAY, 'repeatedly' doubles it and 'round' wraps the pair about the gym class; the preamble's 'uncomplicated' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish rhyming phrase meaning very straightforward, matching the preamble's theme of uncomplicated things.

clue.text: Tease the silly fellow with artistic pretensions

indicators.note: silly suggests letters acting foolishly, so tease and the are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mocking a foolish arty man.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete professes refined appreciation of art and beauty, often affectedly.

clue.text: Misleading tale about this place being heavenly

indicators.note: about wraps the rearranged tale around the place piece
misleading suggests something led astray, so the letters of tale go out of order

parts.note: here means this place

explanation.surface: A deceptive story claims this spot is paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misleading' turns TALE into ETAL, which goes 'about' HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and otherworldly, as if of the heavens.

clue.text: Somewhere like Peterborough said to get wet through

indicators.note: said shows a word is pronounced, and the entry spelt differently

parts.note: the Soke of Peterborough was a historic district of England; a soke is a local jurisdiction

explanation.surface: A Cambridgeshire city reputed to be drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterborough is an English city; its old area was called the Soke of Peterborough.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak is to drench completely in liquid.

clue.text: Hollow son kicking daughter out

indicators.note: kicking with out says one letter is expelled and another takes its place
out completes the phrase, so the daughter letter goes

parts.note: a dimple is a small hollow, in a cheek or surface

explanation.surface: A boy throws his sister out of the house, leaving it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the meaning, uncomplicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for plain and easy, fitting the preamble's theme of uncomplicated things.

clue.text: New pillows, white as seen in a strange night light

indicators.note: new tells us to make the letters of pillows and white fresh by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Fresh white bedding glimpsed in an eerie nocturnal glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a ghostly flickering light over marshes at night, ignis fatuus.

clue.text: Provision for exceptional bedtime story at home

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
in means at home

explanation.surface: A parent arranges a special bedtime tale for a child at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a morning spent in bed longer than usual, an exceptional extra sleep.

clue.text: Rush leaves hanging over river

indicators.note: in a down clue hanging over puts the leaves piece above the river

parts.note: tea is made from leaves

explanation.surface: Foliage drooping over a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to dash along at speed, a verb sense of rush.

clue.text: The last thing a wedding guests expects to eat?

definitions.text: The last thing a wedding guests expects to eat?

parts.words: The last thing a wedding guests expects to eat?
parts.note: the reception ends with slices of the wedding cake handed round

explanation.surface: A wonder at what wedding guests are finally served.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, the phrase also means something very easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of the wedding cake is served last at a reception; the idiom means an easy task.

clue.text: See rebel entering spill drink?

indicators.note: entering means the rebel goes inside the spill

parts.note: a spill is a taper, a thin strip for lighting fires
Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A sight of a revolutionary knocking over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: WAT is Wat Tyler, the English rebel leader of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap water is ordinary drinking water from a household supply.

clue.text: Good money? Continental money inadequate for magnificence

parts.note: the rand is South African currency

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: the euro is the European currency

explanation.surface: Asking about good money, saying European cash falls short of splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and impressiveness of appearance.

clue.text: See beautiful pattern, maybe around insect's wings

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: around turns the art piece back to front

parts.note: a beautiful pattern is an example of art

explanation.surface: Admiring a lovely design round an insect's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Elytra are the hardened forewings of beetles, covering the hind wings.
